dedupe_keys.name: pyciam coastal impacts and adaptation model

description: pyCIAM is the Climate Impact Lab Python implementation of the Coastal Impacts and Adaptation Model, with updates described in the DSCIM-Coastal paper. It calculates coastal losses for regions, years and sea-level-rise scenarios and selects adaptation options from their costs. Users supply socioeconomic and elevation information such as SLIIDERS, sea-level trajectories and a JSON parameter file. Public API functions load inputs, build storm-surge loss tables, calculate costs and select the least-cost adaptation case. The published application is global, while regions, duration and time steps can be configured for other studies. GitHub and PyPI provide the code free under MIT, with notebooks and shell scripts for a small example and full replication. This supports coastal flood-defence investment and climate-adaptation studies. A limitation is sensitivity to exposure and adaptation assumptions. The README also warns that dependencies and testing are still being formalized; larger ensembles require configuring Dask resources. No directly related existing catalogue model was established. This review did not install or execute the model.
